We want to be able to switch between projects with the [ProjectIndicator](.claude/reference/ui/components/project-indicator/ProjectIndicator.md) (as well as just opening an existing project or creating a new one) While any running tasks continue in the background. 

Attached text:

```
background projects (recommended)
Only one project is on screen, but each open project keeps its own running work, and switching back shows it live.
Code changes
The core change is in PromptMode (src/prompt_mode.rs, about 6,150 lines). About 20 of its roughly 45 fields belong to a project, not to the screen:
tasks, working, session, _pending
queue, auto_send, queue_held
asks, answers, ask_session, expanded_ask
history state and steps_shown
Move these into a per-project session object kept in an app-wide map keyed by project folder, and have PromptMode render whichever session is current. Background runs update their own session, never the screen directly. This is a mechanical change, but it touches most of the file. I'd estimate 1,000–2,000 lines changed, mostly self.tasks becoming session.tasks.
Switching stops reloading history when you switch. It only loads a session the first time that project is opened, and keeps it in memory after that.
Quitting (confirm_quit, src/main_window.rs:793) has to count running work in every session, not just the current one.
Builds (piton build from the ribbon) track which project they belong to.
Divergence analysis either becomes per-session too, or gets stopped when you switch. Stopping is simpler, since it's an inset panel.
The project indicator and recent projects show which projects are busy.
No change needed: the language server (restarting per switch is fine), file tree, git panel, editor, palette and settings. They should keep following the current project.
Spec changes
ProjectDirectoryScope: switching changes the project on screen; other projects keep their running work until it finishes.
PromptEditor: tasks, queue and auto-send belong to their project. A project's queue only ever sends into that project.
ChatInputScope: the Ask stack and answer drawer belong to their project. Decide whether the draft text and attachments stay with the project or with you.
HarnessIntegrationScope: already says a conversation is only continued in the project it began in, so it barely changes.
ProjectIndicator and recent projects: a busy marker, and possibly a count of running tasks and questions.
Quitting: the confirmation lists running work across all projects.
DivergenceScope and the ribbon's build: say what happens to a running analysis or build when you switch.
That's about 6–8 scopes, mostly new sections, not rewrites.

```

use /lib
from /ui/components/project-indicator import ProjectIndicator
from /scope/project/open-project import OpenProjectScope
from /scope/new-project import NewProjectScope
from /scope/user-preferences import UserPreferencesScope

export scope ProjectDirectoryScope:
    concept: {ProjectDirectoryConcept}

concept ProjectDirectoryConcept:
    pitch:
        The project the application works on: the directory holding the
        project's piton.config.pi.

    shape: {ProjectDirectoryShape}

shape ProjectDirectoryShape:
    description:
        The application stores the folder holding the project's piton.config.pi
        as the project directory, set when a project is opened with the
        @{OpenProjectScope}, created with the @{NewProjectScope}, or picked
        from the recent projects of the @{ProjectIndicator}. Setting it again
        replaces the project for the whole application.

    recentProjects:
        Every project opened, however it was opened, is remembered among the
        @{UserPreferencesScope}: the five opened most recently, newest first,
        opening one again moving it to the front rather than listing it twice.
        A project that no longer holds its piton.config.pi is left out wherever
        they are offered.
use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/project/open-project import OpenProjectScope
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /scope/no-project import NoProjectStateScope

export ui-component ProjectIndicator:
    concept: {ProjectIndicatorConcept}

concept ProjectIndicatorConcept:
    pitch:
        Shows which project is loaded, at a glance, wherever it sits.

    shape: {ProjectIndicatorShape}

shape ProjectIndicatorShape:
    description:
        A solid block, the full height of wherever it sits, on the same
        background as a text input, the theme's well surface, darker than the
        bar around it in dark mode, with no border and no rounded corners. In it, a small folder icon, then the name
        of the project open through the @{ProjectDirectoryScope}, which is its
        folder's name, in medium weight, vertically centred. The whole block is
        what is clicked, filling it edge to edge, square, and it highlights on
        hover.

    noProject:
        While no project is open, as the @{NoProjectStateScope} says, it reads
        "No project", muted, after the same icon, and has no tooltip.

    tooltip:
        While a project is open, its tooltip gives the project's full path.

    recentProjects:
        Clicking it, or pressing <Ctrl+`> (<Cmd+`> on macOS) anywhere in the
        window, opens a list of the recent projects of the
        @{ProjectDirectoryScope}, up to five, newest first; doing so again closes
        it. Like the palette, the shortcut does nothing while an inset panel is
        open.

        The list hangs flush from the indicator: its top edge is the
        indicator's bottom edge and its left edge the indicator's, at least 360
        pixels wide. It is a solid block in the indicator's own colour, with no
        rounded corners, and a thin edge along its sides and bottom but none
        along its top, where it meets the indicator. While it is open, the rest
        of the window is dimmed as behind an inset panel, and the indicator
        stays undimmed above the dimming, so the two read as one.

        At the top of the list, a filter field with a search icon takes the
        keyboard as the list opens. Typing filters the projects fuzzily, as the
        palette matches, by folder name or full path, the best matches first;
        with nothing typed, all of them show, newest first. <Up> and <Down> move
        a highlight through the rows, wrapping around, starting on the first
        row whenever the filter changes, and <Enter> picks the highlighted row.

        Each project is a row with its folder name in medium weight above its
        full path, muted, after a folder icon, or a tick for the project open
        now. Rows reach the list's edges, with no rounded corners, and highlight
        on hover. Picking a row, by clicking or <Enter>, closes the list and
        opens that project, or just closes it for the one already open.
        Clicking the indicator, clicking the dimmed window, or <Escape> closes
        it.

        The last row, beneath a thin divider, whatever the filter leaves, reads
        "Open Project…" after a folder icon, and closes the list and opens the
        @{OpenProjectScope}.

    width:
        A name wider than 320 pixels is cut off with an ellipsis.

    following:
        It always shows the project open now: opening or creating another
        project changes it straight away.

        message bubbles.

        which heads the view: "No previous tasks", "1 previous task", or
        "N previous tasks". Expanded, the list takes the place of the latest
        task and its output, and the row reads "Back to the latest task".

        its status, with a spinner while it is under way, the name of the
        hidden anchor it was compiled from, and the compiled markdown the
        harness actually received, which scrolls once it gets tall. Until it
        has compiled, the prompt as typed is shown instead.

            @{PromptSendingScope} says, in the order they were sent, and sends
            them one at a time.

        are running beside it when more than one is. Its tooltip says what is
        running, or how many things are. While nothing is, neither shows, and

        task or a question, or while a spec build runs on its own, asks first.

        stops it. The message is titled "Quit while a task is running?" and
        says what is still running: the harness working on a prompt, piton
        build, or both. "Quit" exits, and "Keep Running" or <Escape> dismisses
        it. Asking to quit again while it is open doesn't open a second one,
        and an open palette closes first.

I've planned the change and edited nothing. Your sketch is mostly right. Four corrections:
- **Runs already survive a switch.** `_pending` (the task run), `Ask::_run` and `_history_load` are never dropped when the project changes, and harness.rs only kills the child process when its event receiver is dropped (lines 152–173). So the harness keeps running in the old project today. The bug is that it writes back into whatever is on screen, by `task_ix`.
- **Switching reloads more than history.** The `observe_global::<ProjectDirectory>` handler (prompt_mode.rs:1060) calls `load_queue`, `load_history` and `load_answers`. If the harness is working, `load_history` only sets `history_stale` and waits for the run to end (1461–1492).
- **Not every field is per-project.** `next_ask_id` and `next_queue_id` should stay on PromptMode as app-wide counters. Ids stay unique across projects, so an ask can be found by id alone.
- **Background queues depend on the old-project cleanup check going away.** It matters for divergence too: MainWindow has no project observer today, so nothing stops those panels on a switch.

## 1. Fields (struct at prompt_mode.rs:951–1035)
**Per project → `ProjectSession`:**
- Tasks: `tasks`, `working`, `history_stale`, `_history_load`, `task_history` (a HistoryList, plain data with its own ListState), `_pending`, `session`, `steps_shown` (keyed by task index).
- Queue: `queue`, `queue_expanded`, `auto_send`, `queue_held`.
- Questions: `asks`, `expanded_ask`, `answers`, `ask_history`, `_ask_history_load`, `ask_session`.

**Per screen (stay on PromptMode):**
- Output view: `output_list`, `output_list_for` (keyed by `task.uid`, so it resets itself on a switch, 2770), `output_locked`, `queue_scroll`, `chat_input`.
- File pane: `file`, `pane_opened`, `pane_closing`, `pane_width`, `file_split`, `body_width`, `_file_subscriptions`.
- Drawer: `drawer_share`, `drawer_dragged`, `body_height`, `drawer_height`, `drawer_fill_height`, `stack_rows_height`.
- Other: `selection_popover`, `on_ask_tab`, `next_ask_id`, `next_queue_id`, `summarize`, `_subscriptions`.

**Async write-backs that must target the owning project:**
- **`start` (1696–1880):** the build step, `show_compiled`, `apply_event`, `this.session = …`, `Session::forget`, `task.fail`, and the final `working=false` / `load_history` / `set_busy(false)` / `add_commit_note` / deferred `auto_send_next`.
- **`ask` (1897–2032):** `update_ask(run, …)`, `ask_session`, `expand_ask`.
- **Queue and loads:** `enqueue` → `queue_saved` (1537–1580), and `load_history` / `load_answers`.

All of these already capture `project_dir`. Only the lookup on the way back changes.

## 2. Consumers
- `running_jobs()` (1151) and `is_working()` (1209) read `tasks`, `working` and `asks`.
- `MainWindow::refresh_jobs` (main_window.rs:561) runs on `observe(&prompt_mode)` and the ribbon. It pushes jobs to `Ribbon::set_jobs` (ribbon/mod.rs:214).
- `confirm_quit` (879) uses `is_working()` and `ribbon.is_building()`.
- `reveal_job` (600) calls `reveal_task` / `reveal_question`.
- `Ribbon::build` (spec_tab.rs:262) keeps one `building: bool`.

## 3. Design: a HashMap, not one Entity per project
```rust
struct ProjectSession { /* per-project fields */ }
sessions: HashMap<PathBuf, ProjectSession>,
current: Option<PathBuf>,
empty: ProjectSession, // shown when no project is open
fn session(&self) -> &ProjectSession
fn session_mut(&mut self) -> &mut ProjectSession
fn session_for(&mut self, dir: &Path) -> Option<&mut ProjectSession>
```
Async callbacks do `this.update(cx, |this, cx| { let Some(s) = this.sessions.get_mut(&project_dir) else { return }; …; if this.current.as_deref() == Some(&project_dir) { /* scroll or set_busy */ } cx.notify() })`.

Why not `Entity<ProjectSession>`: the writes are clean, but `apply_event` (1347) mixes session data with screen state (`output_list`, `task_history.expanded`, `output_locked`). Functions like `push_task`, `update_ask` and `steps()` also take `Context<PromptMode>`, and render would need `.read(cx)` at about 110 field sites. That is more churn and more borrow-splitting. The map is the lower-risk option; entities can come later.

**Borrow tip:** `session_mut()` borrows all of `self`. Where screen fields are touched too, index `self.sessions` directly with a cloned key, or compute the screen-side values first.

## Numbered plan
1. **Add the struct, no behaviour change.** Add `ProjectSession` with `ProjectSession::new()` holding the HistoryList builders now in `new()` (1077–1133). Move the fields in, add the accessors, and rewrite every `self.tasks` → `self.session().tasks` (and the other moved fields), about 110 sites including render and `steps()` at 3678. Tests: about 27 `this.<field>` uses become `this.session().…`. Build and test here.
2. **Key write-backs by project.** Change these signatures: `start(project_dir, …)`, `apply_event(dir, ix, event, cx)`, `show_compiled(dir, …)`, `send_next(dir)`, `auto_send_next(dir)`, `queue_saved`, `load_*(dir)`. `apply_event` updates `session_for(dir).tasks[ix]` and only runs the scroll/follow logic when `dir` is current. Output lines for other projects return without notifying.
   - `update_ask(id)` and `close_ask` search every session, since ids are app-wide.
   - `set_busy` only when `dir` is current.
   - `send_next` drops its `ProjectDirectory::get(cx).is_none()` check and uses its own session. Background queues only send `Sending::Queued` items, which are already resolved, so the current project's LSP is never used for another project.
3. **Stop reloading on switch.** Replace the handler at 1060 with `project_changed(cx)`:
   - If the project didn't change, return.
   - Set `current`.
   - If there is no session yet, insert one and run `load_queue`, `load_history`, `load_answers` for it.
   - Set `chat_input.set_busy(session.working)`, clear `selection_popover`, unlock the output, notify.

   Keep `history_stale` per project: it still guards a task sent before the first load lands. In `queue_saved`, the "cancelled while saving" branch becomes "the session exists but the item is gone → remove the file" (the old-project check at 1559 goes away).
4. **Cross-project API.**
   - Keep `running_jobs()` for the current project. Add `busy_projects(&self) -> Vec<ProjectActivity { dir, task: bool, questions: usize, queued: usize }>` for projects with a task running or questions active.
   - `is_working()` covers all projects. Add `working_count()` for the quit dialog.
   - Optional: add `project: Option<PathBuf>` to `Job` (JobKind stays Copy) and `RevealJob(kind, project)`, so revealing a background job switches first.
5. **Builds.** In spec_tab.rs:
   - `building: bool` → `building: HashSet<PathBuf>`.
   - `is_building()` means any build; add `is_building_in(dir)`.
   - `can_build` and the button's loading state check the current project.
   - The callback removes its `dir`, and the notification title names the project when it isn't current.

   Update the `ribbon.building` readers (spec_tab.rs 237–245) and the palette's `can_build` (main_window.rs 928).
6. **Panels.** In `MainWindow::new`, add `cx.observe_global::<ProjectDirectory>` with a `last_project` field. On a real change, call `close_divergence`, `close_rescope`, set `generate_skills = None`, and run `refresh_jobs`.
7. **Quit.** `confirm_quit` counts tasks across projects plus builds, e.g. "The harness is still working in 2 projects."
8. **Indicator.** In `refresh_jobs`, also call `ribbon.project_indicator().update(|pi, cx| pi.set_busy(prompt_mode.busy_projects(), cx))`, merging in the ribbon's building dirs.
   - This follows the existing push pattern, so no global or new event is needed.
   - `ProjectIndicator` gets a `busy: Vec<ProjectActivity>` field.
   - In `render_list` (230–260), busy rows get a spinner or dot and a line like "Task running · 2 questions". The label (`label_contents`) gets a small dot when another project is busy.
   - A busy project not in `recent_projects::openable()` should still be listed; prepend it in `items()`.

## Risks
- **Path keys:** the same folder can arrive in different forms (open_project, recent list, app.rs:32, settings_window:334). Normalize the key (canonicalize, falling back to the raw path) in both `ProjectDirectory::set` and `project_changed`.
- **Ask ids:** `JobKind::Question(id)` must stay unique, so keep `next_ask_id` app-wide.
- **Deferred auto-send (1876):** it must pass `project_dir`, or it would send the queue of whichever project is on screen.
- **Memory:** sessions are never dropped. That's acceptable; optionally drop idle ones that aren't current.
- **Borrow checker:** step 1 is the big mechanical step; do it alone first.
- **`commit_notes::changed` and `harness_mentions::remember`** are keyed by project path already, so they're fine.

## Tests (prompt_mode.rs tests at 3888; helpers `open`, `push_task`, `apply_event`, `push_ask`, `set_working`, `queued_texts`)
- **`background_project_keeps_its_task`:**
  1. Make temp dirs A and B, `open(cx)`, set A.
  2. `ix = push_task("in A")`, `set_working(true)`, apply `TextStarted`.
  3. Set B and `run_until_parked`. Assert `session().tasks` is empty, `is_working()` is true, and `busy_projects()` is `[A]`.
  4. Call `apply_event(&A, ix, TextDelta("hi"))`. B's tasks stay empty.
  5. Set A again. Assert `tasks.len()==1`, the reply text contains "hi", and `session().working` is true.
- **`switching_back_does_not_reload`:** queue a prompt file in A, set A, cancel the item, set B, set A. The queue stays empty and wasn't re-read.
- **Ask in the background:** `start_test_question` in A, switch to B, `update_ask` by id reaches A.
- **main_window tests:**
  - The quit dialog appears when only a background project is working.
  - Divergence closes on a switch.
- **Ribbon test:** a build in A, a switch to B, then `can_build` is true for B.
- **Indicator render test:** a busy row shows its marker (use `test_support` ids like `("recent-project-busy", ix)`).

content.text:
You can now switch projects from the project indicator, or open or create one, and whatever was running in the project you left keeps going in the background. Switching back shows it live, as you left it plus anything that happened since. All 205 tests pass (1 ignored), the only build warning is the old `scroll_y` one, and `piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` pass. I haven't run real harness work across a switch or looked at it on screen; the tests feed simulated harness events.

**What behaves differently now:**
- **Kept per project:** tasks, output, previous tasks, the queue and its auto-send switch, questions, the answer drawer, previous answers, and the conversations both carry on. A run always writes into the project it started in. A project's queue only sends into that project, and keeps sending while it's in the background.
- **Loaded once:** a project's history, answers and queue load the first time it's opened in a launch and stay in memory, so switching back doesn't reload them. The one cost is that projects are never unloaded until you quit.
- **Stays with you:** the prompt being written, its attachments and the selected chat tab. The file tree, Git panel, editor, palette and language server follow whichever project is on screen, as before.
- **Closed on a switch:** a divergence analysis or rescope search stops, and any inset panel closes, since they belong to the screen.
- **Spec builds:** a build keeps running in its own project. Build Spec is only blocked in the project that is building. If it finishes while you're elsewhere, the notification names the project, e.g. "Built 3 files in alpha".
- **Project indicator:** busy projects in the list get a spinner and a line such as "Task running · 2 questions running". A busy project is listed even if it has dropped out of the five recent ones. While another project is busy, a small accent-coloured dot sits after the name and the tooltip says how many.
- **Activity list:** other projects' work is listed after the on-screen project's, e.g. "Task · alpha". Clicking one switches to that project and shows it.
- **Quitting:** it now asks if anything runs in any open project, and says "in N projects" when more than one is involved.
- **Same folder, same project:** a folder reached by different paths now counts as one project.

**How it's built:** I kept the change in `src/prompt_mode.rs` much smaller than your estimate. The per-project fields stay where they were, and on a switch they're swapped out into a per-project store, with the target project's swapped in. When a background run reports back, its project's work is swapped in just for that update, with the scrolling and busy-state effects on screen turned off. This avoided rewriting every field use.

**Spec:** a new `OpenProjectsScope` covers what belongs to a project, what follows the screen, switching, and busy projects. I also updated the Project Directory, Project Indicator, Prompt Editor, Chat Input, Running Activity, Spec Build, Divergence, Rescope and Harness Integration scopes. The spec plan and the code plan agreed; my one call beyond your notes was that draft text and attachments stay with you rather than the project.

**New tests:**
- **`a_project_left_keeps_its_work_running`:** a task and a question run in one project while another is on screen. Background writes land in the right project, and switching back shows them without reloading.
- **`switching_projects_keeps_the_one_left_running`:** covers:
  - a rescope search stopping on a switch;
  - the busy dot and the busy row in the project list;
  - "Question · alpha" in the activity list;
  - Build staying free in the on-screen project;
  - the quit prompt;
  - revealing a job switching back to its project.
